name: Problem with Queries
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$, consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. Your task is to process $$$q$$$ queries of two types: $$$1~p~x$$$ — set the value of the element at index $$$p$$$ equal to $$$x$$$; $$$2~l~r$$$ — count the number of pairs of indices $$$(i, j)$$$ such that $$$l \le i \lt j \le r$$$ and $$$a_i \ne a_j$$$. Note that the queries in this task are encoded ; each subsequent query can only be decoded after calculating the answer to the preceding query of the second type.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^5$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le n$$$). The third line contains a single integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le q \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of queries. The next $$$q$$$ lines describe the queries in one of the following formats: $$$1~p'~x'$$$ ($$$0 \le p', x' \le n-1$$$); $$$2~l'~r'$$$ ($$$0 \le l', r' \le n-1$$$). The queries are encoded as follows: let $$$\mathit{last}$$$ be the answer to the latest processed query of the second type (initially, $$$\mathit{last} = 0$$$). if the type of the query is $$$1$$$, then $$$p = ((p' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1$$$, $$$x = ((x' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1$$$. if the type of the query is $$$2$$$, $$$l = ((l' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1$$$, $$$r = ((r' + \mathit{last}) \bmod n) + 1$$$. If $$$l \gt r$$$, swap their values. Don't forget to update the value of $$$\mathit{last}$$$ after answering each query of the second type. Additional constraint on the input: there is at least one query of the second type.
output_specification: For each query of the second type, print the answer — the number of pairs of indices $$$(i, j)$$$ such that $$$l \le i \lt j \le r$$$ and $$$a_i \ne a_j$$$.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2043G — Problem with Queries [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
